_doc: session-guard config. Copy to session-guard.json (git-ignored) and adjust. `~` expands to the guarded user's home (notify.user, or SUDO_USER when run via sudo) — never to the daemon's own $HOME. Directory prefixes must end with '/'. An allow rule matches when ALL of its specified fields match; prefer team_id/signing_id over bare exe paths (a path can be impersonated, a Developer ID signature cannot). Run `./run.sh --learn 300` to see which processes touch these paths on your machine, then extend `allow`.

allow.name: opencode
allow._note: opencode ships ad-hoc signed (Identifier=a.out, no team) so only its path can be pinned

_allow_examples: Your EDR / antivirus / backup agent will open these files constantly. Find its identity with

notify._user_doc: null = SUDO_USER (run.sh) / baked in by install.sh (LaunchDaemon). Set explicitly if that guess is wrong.
notify._command_doc: optional shell command; receives the alert JSON on stdin (webhook, chat bot, ...)
